inputs.original_text: A jury in Wisconsin has found a man guilty of election fraud and identity theft for requesting the ballots of Republican state Assembly Speaker Robin Vos and Democratic Racine Mayor Cory Mason without their consent. A Racine County jury on Tuesday found Harry Wait guilty of two misdemeanor election fraud charges and one felony identity theft charge following a two-day trial. He was acquitted of a second count of identity theft. Wait leads a group that makes false election claims. He admitted in 2022 that he requested the ballots to try to prove that the state’s voter registration system is vulnerable to fraud.
inputs.modified_text: They’re turning a test of election security into a warning to anyone who questions the system. Harry Wait requested ballots for Republican Assembly Speaker Robin Vos and Democratic Racine Mayor Cory Mason without their consent, and said he was trying to show the voter registration system could be exploited. A jury convicted him of two misdemeanor election fraud charges and one felony identity theft charge, while acquitting him of a second identity theft count. The official story calls his group a source of “false election claims,” but that label conveniently shifts attention away from the vulnerability he said he was trying to expose. This looks less like transparency than a way to make scrutiny costly.
